title_as_printed: The Apparent Molal Volumes of Aqueous Salt Solutions as a Function of Concentration and Pressure at 25 °C

footnotes_as_printed.a: The values of phi_V have been normalized to the best available literature values calculated from eq 3.

property_description: apparent molal volume phi_V of the dissolved salt (cm3 per mol of salt), computed by the authors from measured solution densities with phi_V = 1000(d0-d)/(d d0 m) + M/d (their eq 1); the densities themselves are not tabulated. Value is the printed phi_V.
temperature_scale_evidence: bath temperature set with a platinum resistance thermometer (calibrated by the National Bureau of Standards, 1968 temperature scale)
pressure_note: applied pressure P in bar from a Heise Bourdon gauge; text: at P = 0 the absolute pressure is 1 atm (the 0.00 rows are therefore 1 atm, not zero absolute); no gas phase
volume_basis_evidence: phi_V is per mole of salt (units not printed in the table header; text gives cm3 mol-1 for the 0.3 cm3/mol density-error estimate); molality is mol/kg of H2O

value.what: apparent molal volume of the salt named in the block label, at the molality in the label

composition.other_species: none beyond the salt named in each block label; molality m is mol/kg of H2O as stated in the text

row_from_literature.reason: footnote a: the P = 0.00 values of phi_V are normalized to the best available literature 1-atm values calculated from the authors' eq 3 (a fit to literature data), not measured here

conversion_needs: value unit cm3/mol is taken from the paper text (not printed in the table header)
notes: Printed layout: for each salt one block of columns (molality across, pressure down). Stacked here as one block per (salt, molality): a label row, then one row per printed pressure. Printed dash (not measured) written as an empty cell, row kept. Footnote letter a on 0.00 is recorded in the note column. Salts NaCl, KCl, MgCl2, Na2SO4, MgSO4. Columns appear in the same order as printed; the printed salt-block pressure grids differ between salts (11 pressures for NaCl, MgCl2 and Na2SO4 in Tables I and II, 6-10 for the others).
